channel.title: Stay Safe Online
channel.description: Scams, breaches and online safety, in plain English

item.title: Windows 11 gets November update with search and face login fixes
item.description: Microsoft has released an optional update for Windows 11 that improves search speed and helps facial recognition work in dark rooms.

item.title: Ruby programming language fixes security flaw
item.description: A fix is available for a weakness in Ruby that could allow attackers to disrupt services, though experts say it is hard to exploit.

item.title: F5 issues emergency fixes for critical security flaws
item.description: A major US tech firm has released urgent updates to fix serious weaknesses in its network equipment, which could allow criminals to take control of systems.

item.title: Microsoft now auto-installs Windows 11 26H2 on home PCs
item.description: Microsoft is automatically upgrading eligible personal computers to the latest Windows 11 version, so you may see the update without checking for it yourself.

item.title: New tactic: delivery photo upload failure to steal your parcel
item.description: Criminals are using a new trick to steal parcels by claiming a photo upload failed, leaving shoppers to fight for refunds.

item.title: Careers360 data breach
item.description: Data allegedly taken from the Indian education and careers platform Careers360 appeared on a public hacking forum.

item.title: Why storing work passwords in spreadsheets is risky
item.description: Spreadsheets often miss new or changed passwords, leaving companies unaware of weak or shared logins that attackers can exploit.

item.title: Ofcom lists four ways to check if you are 16 for social media ban
item.description: Ofcom has published a report identifying four reliable methods social media firms can use to verify users are over 16, ahead of the UK's upcoming ban.

item.title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram feature launch
item.description: The UK regulator is checking if Meta broke safety laws by launching a new Instagram feature without assessing risks to children.

item.title: PHP updates fix 18 security flaws, including critical bugs
item.description: The PHP team has released updates to fix 18 security issues, some of which could let attackers control servers.

item.title: WhatsApp fixes flaw that may have been used to make scam messages look real
item.description: WhatsApp has fixed a security gap that scammers may have used to make their messages appear more trustworthy on Android phones.

item.title: Bell Canada confirms data breach affecting business customers
item.description: A Canadian telecoms firm says a hacker stole business contact details, but says no personal passwords or sensitive files were taken.

item.title: Singapore YMCA portal hit by data breach
item.description: The YMCA of Singapore says its online application system was breached, exposing some personal details.

item.title: Microsoft fixes flaw that exposed business contact details
item.description: Microsoft has fixed a security flaw in its Entra Connect Health service that allowed attackers to view some business contact details.

item.title: Rackspace Spot breach exposed customer cloud secrets
item.description: Hackers used stolen login details to access a cloud platform, potentially exposing sensitive passwords and keys for business customers.

item.title: Michigan nurse jailed for Medicare fraud using stolen records
item.description: A nurse in the US was sentenced to prison for billing Medicare for services that never happened, using stolen patient details.

item.title: Criminals use phone calls to steal data from businesses
item.description: A security firm says criminals are using phone calls to steal data.

item.title: Cleverbridge breach exposes payment card details
item.description: Cleverbridge says hackers stole payment card details, including security codes, from its online sales platform.

item.title: Phone company fined £437,500 for letting scammers use its numbers
item.description: Ofcom has fined Tismi for failing to stop scammers from using phone numbers it provided, putting consumers at risk of fraud.

item.title: Ofcom warns about 'job offer' and missed call phone scams
item.description: Criminals are using automated voices and quick hang-ups to trick you into calling back, so you should hang up and report these calls.
